A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ILIAS dataset and benchmarking study. All 23 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices and supplementary figures and tables, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval evaluations, linear-adaptation experiments, re-ranking comparisons and robustness analyses in Sections 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds SigLIP2 results alongside revised re-ranking outcomes.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction procedure, mini-ILIAS distractor selection and proposed linear adaptation remain unchanged. Both versions train a 512-dimensional projection over frozen representations using UnED. Revisions to CS/SP concern benchmark comparators, not the proposed adaptation method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ILIAS objects, queries, positives and distractors, including mini-ILIAS. UnED and its single-domain adaptation subsets, the INSTRE/GLDv2/SOP comparisons, and image-to-image/text-to-image tasks are retained. SigLIP2 adds models without establishing new evaluated domains or languages.

E2.justification: Tables G/H add four SigLIP2 checkpoints: base and large variants trained at resolutions 384 and 512; Table 2 highlights two. Existing comparator families remain, including PCAw, Lw, query expansion, CS, SP and AMES. CS/SP scoring is also revised as described under E3.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the reported CS/SP comparison from local-only scoring to the global/local ensemble used by AMES; v1 discussed ensembling as an additional check. Table G changes USCRR's stated test resolution from 724 to 384. These reported setting changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure J replaces three re-ranking query case studies and revises outcomes for retained examples. The existing analysis questions concerning clutter, scale, adaptation domains, dimensionality and re-ranking memory remain; there is no substantial expansion of the ablation program.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains means and standard deviations over three randomly sampled distractor subsets. Appendix B.2 retains three independent random-seed runs for linear adaptation and the reported standard-deviation range of 0–0.2. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces adapted-SigLIP re-ranking scores: AMES 45.8 to 35.6, CS 38.3 to 32.5, and SP 34.3 to 30.5. Unchanged query expansion at 33.7 now exceeds CS/SP, whose scoring protocol changes. Table F and associated analyses also revise re-ranking outcomes. SigLIP2 adds results reaching 31.3 for adapted image retrieval and 19.8 for text retrieval, while Table G adds unadapted mini-ILIAS scores.

T1.justification: The instance-level relevance definition, view-overlap restriction, mAP@1k definition and adaptation objective remain unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. Restoring the missing 'max' in the existing asymmetric Chamfer description is an explanatory correction.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims about dataset scale, diversity, ground truth, adaptation, local representations and text retrieval. The introduction updates the best global score from 28.9 to 31.3 following SigLIP2 evaluation, without changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 replaces the account of AMES improving the vast majority of queries with explicit acknowledgment that many queries are harmed. It adds failures in sport, gaming and perfume, tentatively linked to landmark-domain training. Appendix A discusses potentially stronger but slower spatial-verification sampling, and Section 5.2 expands the explanation of oracle behavior.

D1.justification: Appendix A explicitly identifies the GLDv2 public split for ensemble tuning and clarifies spatial verification and public AMES resources. Tables G/H document the new SigLIP2 checkpoints and configurations. Appendix D changes the stated license for collected images from CC0 to CC-BY 4.0.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SigLIP2 and Razavian et al.'s Visual instance retrieval with deep convolutional networks, using the latter for Chamfer similarity. Table 1 revises RP2K from fine-grained to partial instance-level and Product1M availability from full to partial. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and terminology corrections and expands re-ranking explanations. Funding and contributor acknowledgments are consolidated and expanded before the references. The main section sequence, appendix organization and most prose remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table G adds a result column and reorders existing columns; Tables 2/G/H gain model rows. Retained plots receive revised ranges and category ordering, and Figure J replaces example panels. Appendix figures D/E exchange numbering and placement, with other local relocations, while the overall visual format remains.

improvement.justification: SigLIP2 comparisons, more consistent re-ranking scoring and clearer failure qualifications provide benefits. However, the new Table G column reports unadapted SigLIP-L trained at 384 scoring 5.7 on mini-ILIAS versus 19.6 on full ILIAS, inconsistent with Section 3.3's subset construction. The PDFs also do not explain the large AMES revisions sufficiently to establish improved accuracy. These unresolved result-reliability issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
